name: Natural
lede: Natural is a pale, warm tan from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, a name so generic it describes almost any unbleached or undyed fiber rather than one specific thing.

sections.title: A name that describes a category, not a thing
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul place this value at plate 11, position A 2, first recorded in 1928 [1]. The same plate position also carries another name in their records, Belleek, from the same year, which our library notes without saying which name came first in use [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 classifies it as a yellowish gray, about 5.8 units from that block's reference chip [2]. Unlike most entries in the dictionary, *natural* names no plant, place or person; it is a trade description, the color of raw linen, wool or paper before dyeing, which is why so many unrelated materials can plausibly claim the name [1].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[tan|Tan]], and it sits close to [[beige|Beige]], [[khaki|Khaki]] and [[camel|Camel]] on the same pale, undyed stretch of the chart [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Natural covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 2,448 works, over one in ten, one of the most common matches we track [3]. It is strongest in paintings from Iran, India, Japan and China, and the painter Xugu carries it in 11 of his 16 archived works [3]. That breadth likely reflects how generic a pale, unbleached tan is at matching aged, varnished grounds and paper, not one pigment or fiber [3]. These remain photographs read as screen colors, not pigment or fiber tests [3].
